The pedestrian’s statement is admissible as an excited utterance because it was made immediately after the accident while the pedestrian was still under the stress of observing it, and the pedestrian’s unavailability or lack of identification does not bar admission under that exception. It is not admissible as a statement of then-existing condition if offered to prove the man’s negligence, since it expresses an opinion about fault rather than a factual observation.  
CONFIDENCE: 70
